{7} ﴿Then whoever seeks beyond that﴾: beyond the wife and the concubine; ﴿those are the transgressors﴾: who exceed what Allah has made lawful to what He has forbidden, those who are bold against the sanctities of Allah. The generality of this verse indicates the prohibition of mut'ah (temporary marriage), for it is not a true wife whose continuance is intended, nor a slave; and it indicates the prohibition of marrying a muhallil (one who marries a divorced woman solely to make her lawful to her former husband). His saying ﴿or what their right hands possess﴾ indicates that for a slave woman to be lawful, all of her must be in his ownership; if he owns only part of her, she is not lawful, because she is not among what his right hand possesses, but is property belonging to him and to another. Just as two husbands may not share a free woman, two masters may not share a female slave.

{8} ﴿And who are keepers of their trusts and their covenant﴾: that is, they observe them, are careful, guard them, and are eager to fulfil and execute them. This is general to all trusts that are a right of Allah and all that are a right of the servants. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it, and man bore it﴾. So all that Allah has obligated upon His servant is a trust upon the servant, whose preservation is by complete performance of it. Likewise, the trusts of human beings enter into this, such as trusts of wealth, secrets, and the like. So it is incumbent upon the servant to observe both matters and to render both trusts: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners﴾. Likewise, covenant (ʿahd) includes the covenant between them and their Lord and that between them and the servants, namely the obligations and contracts that the servant enters into. So it is incumbent upon him to observe them and fulfil them, and it is forbidden for him to neglect or disregard them.

{9} ﴿And who are attentive to their prayers﴾: that is, they persist in them at their times, within their limits, their prescribed conditions, and their pillars. So He praised them for humble focus in prayer and for guarding it, because their affair is not complete except by both matters. Whoever persists in prayer without humble focus, or has humble focus without guarding it, is blameworthy and deficient.

{10} ﴿Those﴾: described by those qualities ﴿are the inheritors﴾.

{11} ﴿Who will inherit al-Firdaws﴾: which is the highest, middle, and best part of Paradise, because they are adorned with the highest and peak of the qualities of good. Or the intended meaning is the whole of Paradise, so that the generality of believers enters it according to their degrees in ranks, each according to his condition. ﴿They will abide therein forever﴾: they will not depart from it nor desire any change from it, because it comprises the most complete, excellent, and perfect bliss, without any troubling or disturbance.

Allah mentions in these verses the stages of the human being and his transitions from the beginning of his creation to the final state he reaches:

{12} He then mentions the beginning of the creation of the father of the human race, Adam (peace be upon him), and that he was made "from an extract of clay." That is, he was extracted and taken from all of the earth. Therefore his offspring came in accordance with the earth's variety: some of them good and some evil, and others between these; some easygoing and some sorrowful, and others between these.

{13} "Then We placed him" — that is, the species of human beings — "as a sperm-drop (nutfah), lodged in a firm place (qarar makin)": it issues from between the loins and the ribs and settles "in a firm place," which is the womb, protected from corruption, wind, and other things.

{14} "Then We made the sperm-drop" that had settled "into a clot ('alaqah)": that is, into red blood after forty days have passed since the sperm-drop. Then "We made the clot" — after another forty days — "into a lump of flesh (mudghah)": that is, a small piece of flesh about the size that one can chew, given its smallness. "Then We made the lump" — the soft one — "into bones," solid bones that were interlaced with the flesh according to the body's need for them. "Then We clothed the bones with flesh": that is, We made the flesh a covering for the bones, just as We made the bones a support for the flesh, and this occurs in the third forty days. "Then We produced him as another creation": He breathed the spirit into him, and he passed from being inanimate to becoming a living being. "So blessed is Allah," that is, He is exalted, magnified, and abundant in good, "the best of creators": "He who made good everything He created, and began the creation of man from clay. Then He made his offspring from an extract of worthless fluid. Then He proportioned him and breathed into him of His spirit, and made for you hearing, sight, and hearts; little are you grateful." So all of His creation is good, and man is among the best of His creatures, indeed he is the best of them absolutely, as Allah, the Exalted, says: "We have certainly created man in the best of stature." For this reason, his distinguished ones are the most excellent and most perfect of creatures.

{15} "Then indeed you, after that" — the creation and the breathing of the spirit — "will surely die" at one of your stages and transitions.

{16} "Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be resurrected," and you will be recompensed for your deeds, good and bad. Allah, the Exalted, says: "Does man think he will be left neglected? Was he not a sperm-drop emitted? Then he was a clot, and He created and proportioned, and made of him two sexes, the male and the female. Is not He then able to give life to the dead?"

{17} When God mentioned the creation of man, He mentioned his dwelling and the abundance of blessings bestowed upon him from every direction, saying: ﴿And We have created above you﴾: a ceiling for the lands and a benefit for the servants, ﴿seven heavens﴾; that is, seven heavens layered one above another, each level above the other, adorned with stars, the sun and the moon, and containing whatever benefits for creation He placed in them. ﴿And We are never unaware of the creation﴾. Just as Our creating encompasses every creature, Our knowledge also encompasses what We have created. We do not overlook any creature or forget it, nor do We create a creature and then neglect it. We do not let the sky fall upon the earth, nor do We forget a particle in the depths of the seas, the far reaches of the deserts, or any creature without sending its provision to it. ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that its provision is upon God, and He knows its resting place and its storage place﴾. God often links His creating with His knowing, as in His saying: ﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾, and ﴿Yes, indeed; He is the Creator, the All-Knowing﴾, because the creation of created things is among the strongest rational proofs of the knowledge and wisdom of their Creator.

{18} ﴿And We sent down water from the sky﴾: to be a provision for you and your livestock, in an amount sufficient for you. He does not reduce it [so that it would not suffice for the earth and the trees, and the purpose would not be achieved], nor does He increase it beyond what can be borne, so that it would destroy dwellings and plants and trees could not live from it. Rather, He sends it down at the time of need for it, then diverts it when its continuation would cause harm. ﴿Then We caused it to settle in the earth﴾; that is, We sent it down upon the earth, so it settled, remained, and by the power of its Sender produced all kinds of plants. He also caused it to settle, prepared in the storehouses of the earth, such that it does not go off downward so that it cannot be reached or its bottom cannot be attained. ﴿And indeed, We are able to take it away﴾: either by not sending it down, or by sending it down and having it go off downward where it cannot be reached, or by its not producing the purpose for which it was intended. This is a reminder from Him to His servants that they should thank Him for His blessing and consider its absence: what harm would result from it. This is like His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered: if your water should sink away, who would bring you flowing water?﴾.

{19} ﴿Then We produced for you by it﴾; that is, by that water, ﴿gardens﴾; that is, orchards ﴿of palm trees and grapevines﴾. God singled out these two kinds, although other trees also grow from it, because of their excellence and their benefits, by which they surpass other trees. For this reason He mentioned the general term in His saying ﴿for you﴾; that is, in those gardens there are many fruits, of which you eat, such as figs, citrons, pomegranates, apples, and others.

{20} ﴿And a tree that grows out of Mount Sinai﴾: this is the olive tree; that is, its species. It is singled out for mention because its place is specific, in the land of al-Sham, and because of its benefits, some of which are mentioned in His saying: ﴿yielding oil and a relish for those who eat﴾; that is, in it is oil, which is an ointment, used for its use in lighting lamps, and as a condiment for those who eat, that is, it is made into a sauce for those who eat, along with other benefits.

{21} That is: among His blessings upon you is that He subjected the livestock to you—the camels, cattle and sheep—in which there is a lesson for those who take heed and benefits for those who seek benefit. {We give you to drink of what is in their bellies}: milk that comes out from between waste matter and blood, pure and palatable to those who drink it. {And for you therein are many benefits}: from their wool, their fur and their hair. He also made for you, from the hides of the livestock, dwellings that you find light to carry on the day of your travelling and the day of your settling down. {And from them you eat}: the finest of foods, of meat and fat.

{22} {And upon them and upon ships you are carried}; that is: He made them (the animals) as ships for you on land, on which you carry your loads to a land you could not have reached except with great hardship; just as He made ships for you on the sea, to carry you and your goods, whether little or much. So He who has bestowed these blessings, arranged the kinds of kindness, and poured down upon us from His abundant goodness, is the One who deserves complete gratitude, complete praise, and striving in His worship, and that His blessings not be used as aid in disobeying Him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 23, verses 42–44:

{42–43} Meaning: Then after these deniers, the obstinate opponents, We produced {other generations}: each nation at a appointed time and a set term, neither advancing from it nor delaying. We sent to them successive messengers, perhaps they would believe and turn back in repentance. Disbelief and denial remained the custom of the disobedient nations and the defiant disbelievers, {every time a messenger came to a nation, they denied him}, even though every messenger came with signs such that people would believe on the like of them. Indeed, the mere call of the messengers and their law indicates the truth of what they brought.

{44} {Then We made them follow one another}: with destruction, so none of them remained, and their dwellings became empty after them. {And We made them tales}: people speak of them after them, and they become a lesson for the God-fearing, a deterrent for the deniers, and a disgrace upon them coupled with their punishment. {So away with the people who do not believe}: how wretched they are! May they perish! How losing their bargain is!

For a long time I have come across a statement of some scholars, whose name does not come to mind now, that after [the sending of] Moses and the descent of the Torah, God lifted the punishment of annihilation from the nations, and prescribed jihad against the obstinate deniers. I did not know where he had taken it from. But when I reflected on these verses together with the verses in Surah al-Qasas, its meaning became clear to me. As for these verses, God mentioned the nations destroyed one after another in succession to destruction, then informed that He sent Moses after them and sent down to him the Torah, in which there is guidance for people. The destruction of Pharaoh does not conflict with this, for it occurred before the descent of the Torah.

As for the verses in Surah al-Qasas, they are very explicit, for when He mentioned the destruction of Pharaoh, He said: {And We certainly gave Moses the Book after We had destroyed the former generations, as insight for the people, and guidance and mercy, that they might remember}. This is explicit that He gave him the Book after the destruction of the rebellious nations, and informed that He sent it down as insight for people, and guidance and mercy.

Perhaps from this is what God mentioned in Surah Yunus, in His saying: {Then after him We sent messengers to their peoples}, i.e., after Noah, {and they brought them clear proofs, but they were not going to believe in what they had denied before. Thus do We seal the hearts of the transgressors. Then after them We sent Moses and Aaron...}, the verses. And God knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 23, verse 51–56:

{51} This is a command from Allah, exalted is He, to His messengers to eat of the good things (al-tayyibat), which are: provision, and that which is good and lawful, along with thanking Allah through righteous deeds, by which the heart, the body, this world and the Hereafter are set right. He informs them that He is All-Aware of what they do; so every deed they performed and every effort they exerted, Allah knows it, and He will reward them for it with the most complete and the best reward. This indicates that all the messengers agree on the permissibility of good foods and the prohibition of the foul (al-khaba'ith) among them, and that they agree on every righteous deed, even though some kinds of commanded acts vary and the sharia (shara'i') differ in them; for they are all righteous deeds, but they vary according to the variation of times. Therefore, the righteous deeds that are good in all times have been agreed upon by the prophets and the sharia: such as the command to affirm the oneness of Allah (tawhid), to devote the religion sincerely to Him, to love Him, to fear Him and to hope in Him, to piety and truthfulness, to fulfilling covenants, to maintaining the ties of kinship, to being dutiful to parents, to kindness toward the weak, the needy and orphans, to compassion and benevolence toward creation, and similar righteous deeds. For this reason, when Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ), the people of knowledge, the earlier scriptures and reason would derive evidence for his prophethood from the kinds of things he commanded and forbade, as happened with Heraclius and others; for when he commanded what the prophets before him commanded and forbade what they forbade, this indicates that he is of their kind. This is unlike the liar, who must command evil and forbid good.

{52} For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said to the messengers: ﴿Indeed, this community of yours is one community﴾; that is, your religious community, O messengers, ﴿one﴾: agreed upon one religion, and your Lord is One. ﴿So fear Me﴾: by carrying out My commands and avoiding My prohibitions. Allah has commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, because they are the ones the believers follow and after whom they walk, so He said: ﴿O you who have believed, eat of the good things We have provided for you, and be thankful to Allah if it is Him you worship﴾. Therefore it is obligatory on all who are affiliated with the prophets, and others, to comply with this and act upon it.

{53} But the wrongdoers who divided refused except rebellion. For this reason He said: ﴿So they divided their affair among themselves into sects﴾; that is, those affiliated with the followers of the prophets divided their affair, which is their religion, ﴿among themselves into sects﴾; that is, into pieces. ﴿Each faction, with what they have, rejoicing﴾; that is, with what they possess of knowledge and religion. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 23, verse 72:

{72} That is: Did it prevent them from following you, O Muhammad, that you ask them for a reward for responding? ﴿Or do you ask them for any payment? But the payment of your Lord is better, and He is the best of providers.﴾ Rather, they are burdened with a debt from following you, because of what you take from them as wages and tribute. The matter is not so. ﴿But the payment of your Lord is better, and He is the best of providers.﴾ This is like what the prophets said to their peoples: ﴿O my people, I do not ask you for any wealth for it; my reward is only from Allah﴾. That is: they do not call people out of desire for the wealth that would come to them from them, but they call them out of sincere advice for them and to secure their welfare. Indeed, the messengers were more sincere to creation than their own selves. So may Allah reward them on behalf of their peoples with the best of rewards, and grant us the ability to follow them in all circumstances.

{75} This is an explanation of the intensity of their rebellion and obstinacy: that when harm afflicts them, they call upon God to remove it from them so that they may believe, or He tests them with it so that they may return to Him; yet when God removes the harm from them, they {persist} (lajju), meaning they continue {in their transgression, wandering blindly} (ya'mahun), that is, they roam about in their disbelief, bewildered and hesitant. This is like what God mentioned of their state when they board the ship, when they call upon Him, making their religion sincerely His, and forget what they associate with Him; then when He delivers them, behold, they commit injustice (yabghun) in the earth through association and otherwise.

{76} {And We certainly seized them with punishment}: The exegetes said: what is meant by this is the famine that afflicted them for seven years, and that God tested them with it so that they would return to Him in humility and submission, but it did not benefit them, nor did any of them succeed. {So they did not humble themselves before their Lord}, meaning they did not submit and were not abased, {nor did they supplicate}: to Him, nor implore Him, but rather that affliction passed over them and then ceased as if it had never touched them, and they remained in their error and disbelief.

{77} But behind them lies the punishment that cannot be averted, and it is His saying: {until when We open upon them a gate of severe punishment}, such as the killing on the day of Badr and other than it; {then behold, they will be in despair therein}: hopeless of every good, with evil and its causes present to them. So let them beware before the descent of God's severe punishment, which cannot be turned back; unlike mere punishment, for it may be lifted from them, like the worldly penalties with which God disciplines His servants. God the Exalted said concerning them: {Corruption has appeared on land and sea by what the hands of people have earned, that He may let them taste part of that which they have done, so that they might return} (Q. 30:41).

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 23, verses 78–80:

{78} He, may He be exalted, informs of His favours upon His servants, calling them to thank Him and to fulfil the duty owed to Him, saying: ﴿And it is He who produced for you hearing and sight and hearts﴾. [He gave you hearing] so that you may perceive audible things and benefit thereby in your religion and your worldly affairs; [and sight] so that you may perceive visible things and benefit thereby in your interests; [and hearts], i.e., the intellects (al-'uqul) by which you perceive things and are distinguished from the beasts. So if you were deprived of hearing, sight and intellect, being deaf, blind and mute, what would your condition be? And what would you lack of your necessities and your perfection? Will you not then give thanks to the One who bestowed upon you these blessings, so that you establish His Oneness and obey Him? Ibn Sa'di's commentary on surah 23, verses 81–83:

{81–83} That is: rather, these deniers followed the path of the earlier deniers of the Resurrection, found it extremely improbable, and said: ﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we truly be raised again?﴾ That is, in their view this cannot be conceived and does not fit within reason. ﴿We and our forefathers have indeed been promised this before.﴾ That is, we have continually been promised that the Resurrection will take place, both we and our forefathers, yet we have not seen it, and it has not yet come. ﴿This is nothing but the myths of the ancients.﴾ That is, their tales and evening stories which are recounted for entertainment; apart from this, they have no reality. They lied, may Allah disfigure them. For Allah has shown them signs of His greater than the Resurrection, and similar to this is His saying: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾, and His saying: ﴿And he presents to Us a parable and forgets his own creation, saying: "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ and the verses that follow, and His saying: ﴿And you see the earth lifeless, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells﴾ and the verses that follow.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 23, verses 84–89:**

{84–85} That is: Say to these deniers of the Resurrection, who associate others with Allah, arguing against them with what they themselves affirm and acknowledge of *tawhid al-rububiyyah* (the oneness of Lordship, i.e., that Allah alone is the Lord and Creator) and of Allah's sole possession of it, against what they deny of *tawhid al-uluhiyyah* (the oneness of divinity and worship). And [argue] with what they affirm of the creation of the great created things, against what they deny of the restoration of the dead, which is easier than that: ﴿To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it?﴾ That is: Who is the Creator of the earth and of what is on it, of animals, plants, inanimate things, seas, rivers and mountains, who owns all of that and manages it? For if you ask them about this, they will certainly say: "Allah alone." So say to them, when they acknowledge that: ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ That is: Will you not return to what Allah has reminded you of, which is known to you and settled in your innate nature (*fitar*, the natural disposition), though heedlessness may obscure it at some times? The truth is that if you return to your memory through mere reflection, you will know that the owner of all this is the one God worthy of worship, and that the divinity of one who is himself owned is the greatest falsehood.

{86–87} Then he moved on to what is greater than that, saying: ﴿Say: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens﴾, with what is in them of luminous bodies, wandering planets and fixed stars, ﴿and the Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾, which is the highest, widest and greatest of created things. Who created and managed all of that and directed it with various kinds of management? ﴿They will say: "To Allah."﴾ That is: They will acknowledge that Allah is the Lord of all of that. Say to them, when they acknowledge that: ﴿Will you not then fear Allah?﴾ Will you worship created things that are powerless, and not fear the great Lord, of perfect power and mighty dominion?! In this there is a gentleness of address, in His saying ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ and ﴿Will you not then fear Allah?﴾, and in the exhortation through the particle of invitation, which attracts hearts, there is something that is not hidden.

{88–89} Then he moved on to their acknowledgment of what is more comprehensive than all of that, saying: ﴿Say: In whose hand is the dominion (*malakut*, a form of intensification meaning sovereignty) of everything?﴾ That is: the dominion of everything in the upper world and the lower world, what we see and what we do not see. ﴿And He gives protection﴾ to His servants from evil, averts hateful things from them, and guards them from what harms them. ﴿And none can be protected against Him.﴾ That is: no one can grant protection against Allah, or repel the evil that Allah has decreed. Indeed, no one can intercede with Him except by His permission. ﴿They will say: "To Allah."﴾ That is: they will acknowledge that Allah is the owner of everything, the Protector against whom no one can be given protection. ﴿Say﴾ to them, when they acknowledge that, as a binding argument against them: ﴿Then how are you deluded?﴾ That is: Where do your minds go, when you worship those whom you know have no dominion and no share of dominion, who are powerless in every respect, and abandon sincere devotion to the Owner, the Mighty, the Able, the Manager of all affairs? The minds that guided you to this must be bewitched, and undoubtedly Satan has bewitched them with what he made attractive to them, beautified for them, and inverted the realities for them, so he bewitched their minds, just as the sorcerers bewitched the eyes of the people.

Who created and managed all of that and directed it with various kinds of management? ﴿They will say: "To Allah."﴾ That is: They will acknowledge that Allah is the Lord of all of that. Say to them, when they acknowledge that: ﴿Will you not then fear Allah?﴾ Will you worship created things that are powerless, and not fear the great Lord, of perfect power and mighty dominion?! In this there is a gentleness of address, in His saying ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ and ﴿Will you not then fear Allah?﴾, and in the exhortation through the particle of invitation, which attracts hearts, there is something that is not hidden.

{88–89} Then he moved on to their acknowledgment of what is more comprehensive than all of that, saying: ﴿Say: In whose hand is the dominion (*malakut*, a form of intensification meaning sovereignty) of everything?﴾ That is: the dominion of everything in the upper world and the lower world, what we see and what we do not see. ﴿And He gives protection﴾ to His servants from evil, averts hateful things from them, and guards them from what harms them. ﴿And none can be protected against Him.﴾ That is: no one can grant protection against Allah, or repel the evil that Allah has decreed. Indeed, no one can intercede with Him except by His permission. ﴿They will say: "To Allah."﴾ That is: they will acknowledge that Allah is the owner of everything, the Protector against whom no one can be given protection. ﴿Say﴾ to them, when they acknowledge that, as a binding argument against them: ﴿Then how are you deluded?﴾ That is: Where do your minds go, when you worship those whom you know have no dominion and no share of dominion, who are powerless in every respect, and abandon sincere devotion to the Owner, the Mighty, the Able, the Manager of all affairs? The minds that guided you to this must be bewitched, and undoubtedly Satan has bewitched them with what he made attractive to them, beautified for them, and inverted the realities for them, so he bewitched their minds, just as the sorcerers bewitched the eyes of the people.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 23, verse 90–92:

{90–92} Allah, the Exalted, says: Rather, We have brought to these deniers of the truth that which contains truthfulness in the reports and justice in the commands and prohibitions. So what is wrong with them that they do not acknowledge it, when it is more deserving of being followed, and they have nothing to replace it with except lying and wrongdoing? For this reason He said: ﴿And indeed, they are liars. Allah has not taken any son, and there is not with Him any god.﴾ This is a lie that is known from the report of Allah and the report of His messengers, and it is known by sound reason. For this reason, the Exalted drew attention to the rational proof for the impossibility of two gods, saying: ﴿Otherwise﴾, that is, if there were with Him other gods as they claim, ﴿each god would have taken away what he created﴾, that is, each of the two gods would have been independent with his creatures and would have sovereignly managed them, and would have been eager to prevent the other and overpower him, ﴿and some of them would have prevailed over others.﴾ So the dominant one would be the god. With mutual opposition, the existence of the world would not be possible, nor could it be conceived that it would be arranged in this astonishing order that amazes minds. Consider this with the sun, the moon, the fixed stars and the wandering planets: from the time they were created, they have been running on one system and one arrangement, all of them subjected by power and governed by wisdom for the benefit of all creation, not restricted to the benefit of one over another, and you will never see in them any defect, contradiction, or opposition in the slightest action. So is it conceivable that this arrangement is the decree of two lord-gods? ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they describe.﴾ They have spoken with the tongue of their state and conveyed through their wondrous forms that the one who manages them is one God, perfect in His names and attributes, to whom all creatures are in need in His lordship over them and in His divinity over them. Just as there is no existence or permanence for them except by His lordship, so there is no well-being or sustenance for them except by worshipping Him and devoting obedience to Him alone. For this reason, He drew attention to the greatness of His attributes through an example of that, which is His all-encompassing knowledge, saying: ﴿Knower of the unseen﴾, that is, what has been hidden from our sight and knowledge of the obligatory, the impossible and the possible, ﴿and the witnessed﴾, which is what we observe of that. ﴿Exalted is He﴾, that is, He is elevated and magnified ﴿above what they associate﴾ with Him. And they have no knowledge except what Allah has taught.

{96} This is among the noble character traits which Allah commanded His Messenger to adopt, saying: {Repel evil with that which is better} (23:96). That is: if your enemies wrong you with words and deeds, do not repay them with wrongdoing. Although it is permissible to punish the wrongdoer with the like of his wrong, repel their wrong toward you with kindness from you toward them, for that is a favor from you upon the wrongdoer. Among the benefits of this is that the wrong is lightened from you both in the present and in the future, and that it is more effective in bringing the wrongdoer to the truth, closer to his regret and remorse, and his returning in repentance from what he has done. The one who pardons is characterized by the quality of goodness, subdues through this his enemy Satan, and earns reward from the Lord. Allah the Exalted said: {So whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with Allah} (42:40). And Allah the Exalted said: {Repel evil with that which is better; then indeed, the one between whom and you there is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend. But none is granted this except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune} (41:34–35). That is: none is enabled to this beautiful character except those who are patient.

And His saying: {We are most knowing of what they describe} (23:96): that is, of what they say of statements that contain disbelief and denial of the truth. Our knowledge encompasses that. We have shown forbearance toward them, granted them respite, and been patient with them, and the right is ours, and their denial is of us. So you, O Muhammad, should be patient with what they say and repay them with goodness. This is the duty of the servant in response to the wrongdoer among mankind.

{97–98} As for the wrongdoer among the devils, kindness does not benefit with him, and he calls his party only so that they may become among the companions of the blaze. So the duty in confronting him is to seek guidance by what Allah guided His Messenger to, so He said: {And say, "My Lord, I seek refuge in You} [i.e., I seek protection by Your power and strength, disclaiming my own power and strength] {from the incitements of the devils. And I seek refuge in You, My Lord, lest they be present with me"} (23:97–98). That is: I seek refuge in You from the evil that befalls me through their direct contact, their incitement, and their touch, and from the evil that comes through their presence and their whispering. This is a seeking of refuge from the root and source of all evil, and it includes seeking refuge from all the prods of Satan and from his touch and his whispering. So when Allah grants refuge to His servant from this evil and answers his supplication, he is safe from every evil and is enabled to every good.

Ibn Sa'di's commentary on surah 23, verses 99–100:

{99–100} He, exalted is He, informs us about the condition of those among the negligent and wrongdoers whom death attends: that in that state he will regret when he sees his destination and witnesses the ugliness of his deeds, so he asks to return to the world, not in order to enjoy its pleasures and pluck its desires, but rather he says: ﴿My Lord, send me back, that I may do righteous deeds in what I have left behind.﴾ [of] the deeds, and I neglected my duty toward Allah. ﴿No!⌋ That is, there is no return for him and no respite. Allah has decreed that they will not be returned to it. ﴿Indeed, it is but a word he is saying⌋ That is, his statement in which he wishes to return to the world is ﴿but a word he is saying﴾, meaning a mere utterance of the tongue, which benefits its speaker only with regret and remorse. He is also not truthful in it, for if he were returned he would go back to what he was forbidden from. ﴿And behind them is a barrier (barzakh) until the Day they are resurrected.﴾ That is, before them, in front of them, there is a barzakh, which is the barrier between two things. Here it is the barrier between the worldly life and the Hereafter. In this barzakh the obedient enjoy bliss and the disobedient are punished from their death until the Day they are resurrected. So let them prepare its provision and take its readiness.

So let them prepare its provision and take its readiness.

{101} Allah, the Exalted, informs us of the terror of the Day of Resurrection and of the distressing and frightening things in that Day. When the Trumpet is blown for the Resurrection, all of mankind will be gathered for the appointed time of a known Day. The terror of that Day will befall them to such an extent that it will make them forget their lineages, which are the strongest of the means of connection, and so everything else is forgotten by a fortiori reasoning. No one will ask another about his condition, because each will be preoccupied with himself. He will not know whether he will be saved with a salvation after which there is no wretchedness, or whether he will be wretched with a wretchedness after which there is no happiness. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿But when the Deafening Blast comes, on the Day a man will flee from his brother, his mother and his father, his spouse and his children, each man that Day will have a matter that occupies him fully﴾.

{102} In the Hereafter there are stations whose distress is intense and whose impact is great, such as the Scale by which the deeds of the servant are weighed. By it his deeds are measured with justice, what is for him and what is against him is examined, and the weights of the smallest particles of good and evil become distinguished. ﴿Then whoever's scales are heavy﴾: meaning, whose good deeds outweigh his bad deeds. ﴿Those are the successful﴾: because they are saved from the Fire, deserve Paradise, and win praiseworthy commendation.

{103} ﴿And whoever's scales are light﴾: meaning, whose bad deeds outweigh his good deeds, and whose sins surround them. ﴿Those are the ones who have lost themselves﴾: every loss other than this loss is, by comparison with it, easy. This loss is a hard one, whose calamity cannot be repaired and whose missed opportunity cannot be recovered. It is an everlasting loss and a perpetual wretchedness, in which a person has lost his noble self, by which he could have attained eternal happiness, and so he has forfeited this everlasting bliss in the presence of the Generous Lord. ﴿Abiding in Hell﴾: they will not leave it, forever and ever. This threat, as we have mentioned, applies only to those whose sins surround their good deeds, and that does not occur except for a disbeliever. Accordingly, such a person is not reckoned in the manner of one whose good and bad deeds are weighed, for they have no good deeds. Rather, their deeds are counted and enumerated, and they are made to stand before them, are made to acknowledge them, and are humiliated by them.

As for the one who has the root of faith with him, but whose sins are great so that they outweigh his good deeds, he, although he enters the Fire, will not remain in it forever, as the texts of the Book and the Sunnah (the prophetic tradition) indicate.

{104} Then Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the evil end of the disbelievers, saying: ﴿The Fire scorches their faces﴾: meaning, it envelops them from all their sides, until it reaches their noble limbs, and its flames come right up to their faces. ﴿And they therein are grim-faced﴾: their faces are contorted and their lips shrink back, because of the intensity of what they are in and the magnitude of what they encounter.

{105} Then it will be said to them, as rebuke and reproach: ﴿Were not My verses recited to you?﴾: by which you were called to believe, and which were presented to you so that you might reflect. ﴿And you used to deny them﴾: out of your injustice and obstinacy, though they are clear signs that distinguish truth from falsehood and make plain the one who is right from the one who is wrong.

{106} Then they will acknowledge their wrongdoing at a time when acknowledgment will not benefit them. ﴿They will say: "Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us"﴾: meaning, the wretchedness arising from injustice, from turning away from the truth, from inclining toward what harms, and from abandoning what benefits, overcame us. ﴿And we were a people astray﴾: in their deeds, even though they knew that they were wrongdoers. That is, in the world we acted like the bewildered, misguided, foolish one, as they said in another verse: ﴿And they will say, "Had we been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze."﴾

{107} ﴿"Our Lord, bring us out of it, and if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers."﴾ But they are lying in this promise of theirs, for, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden.﴾ Allah did not leave them any argument; rather, He cut off their excuses, and He gave them in the world a lifespan in which whoever would remember could remember, and in which the criminal could be restrained.

{108} Then Allah answers their request: ﴿"Be silent in it, and do not speak to Me."﴾ This statement, from which we seek Allah's protection, is the greatest statement absolutely that the criminals will hear, in its disappointment, rebuke, humiliation, loss, and despair of every good, and its announcement of every evil. This speech and this anger from the Merciful Lord are harsher upon them and more effective in their torment than the torment of the Blazing Fire.

{109} Then He mentioned the condition that led them to punishment and cut off mercy from them, saying: ﴿Indeed, there was a group of My servants who said, "Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of the merciful."﴾ They combined faith, which necessitates righteous deeds, with supplication to their Lord for forgiveness and mercy, and with seeking nearness to Him through His lordship and His favor upon them in guiding them to faith, and with acknowledgment of the vastness of His mercy and the generality of His kindness. Implicit in this is what indicates their submission, humility, brokenness before their Lord, fear, and hope. These are the masters of mankind and their virtuous ones.

{110} ﴿But you took them in mockery﴾: O disbelievers, base and wretched, deficient in intellect and forbearance. ﴿Until they made you forget My remembrance, and you used to laugh at them﴾: this that caused them to forget the remembrance was their preoccupation with mocking them, just as their forgetting the remembrance urges them on to mockery. Each of the two matters feeds the other. So is there any boldness beyond this boldness?

{111} ﴿Indeed, I have rewarded them today for their patience﴾: in obeying Me and in bearing your harm, until they reached Me. ﴿That it is they who are the victorious﴾: with everlasting bliss and deliverance from the Hellfire. As He said in another verse: ﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers…﴾ and the verses that follow.

{112–114} He says to them, in a manner of reproach and as a way of calling them foolish of intellect, since in this brief period they acquired every evil that led them to His anger and His punishment, and did not acquire what the believers acquired of good that leads them to lasting happiness and the pleasure of their Lord: ﴿"How many years did you remain on the earth?" They said, "We remained a day or part of a day."﴾ Their statement is based on their extreme underestimation of the length of their stay in the world. This indicates it, but it does not specify its quantity or define it. Therefore they said: ﴿So ask those who count﴾: meaning, those who keep account of its number. {110} ﴿But you took them in mockery﴾: O disbelievers, base and wretched, deficient in intellect and forbearance. ﴿Until they made you forget My remembrance, and you used to laugh at them﴾: this that caused them to forget the remembrance was their preoccupation with mocking them, just as their forgetting the remembrance urges them on to mockery. Each of the two matters feeds the other. So is there any boldness beyond this boldness?

{111} ﴿Indeed, I have rewarded them today for their patience﴾: in obeying Me and in bearing your harm, until they reached Me. ﴿That it is they who are the victorious﴾: with everlasting bliss and deliverance from the Hellfire. As He said in another verse: ﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers…﴾ and the verses that follow.

{112–114} He says to them, in a manner of reproach and as a way of calling them foolish of intellect, since in this brief period they acquired every evil that led them to His anger and His punishment, and did not acquire what the believers acquired of good that leads them to lasting happiness and the pleasure of their Lord: ﴿"How many years did you remain on the earth?" They said, "We remained a day or part of a day."﴾ Their statement is based on their extreme underestimation of the length of their stay in the world. This indicates it, but it does not specify its quantity or define it. Therefore they said: ﴿So ask those who count﴾: meaning, those who keep account of its number. As for them, they are occupied with a preoccupying distraction and a stupefying torment, which keeps them from knowing its number. So He said to them: ﴿"You remained not but a little, if you had known."﴾ Whether you determine its number or not.

{115–116} That is: "Did you then think" (O creatures) "that We created you in vain," meaning purposelessly and falsely, that you would eat, drink, frolic, and enjoy the pleasures of this world, and that We would leave you without commanding you, without forbidding you, and without rewarding or punishing you? For this reason He said: "and that to Us you would not be returned?" This does not occur to your minds. "Exalted is Allah," meaning He is magnified and elevated above this false assumption, which leads to a disparagement of His wisdom. "The True King; there is no deity except Him, the Lord of the Mighty Throne." His being the King of all creation in truth, in His true statements, His promise, and His threat, and His being the one worthy of worship (ma'luh, ma'bud) because of the perfection that belongs to Him, the Lord of the Mighty Throne and what is below it, is all the more reason that He would prevent Himself from creating you in vain.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 23, verses 117–118:

{117} That is: whoever calls upon another god alongside Allah, without any evidence (bayyinah) regarding it or any proof (burhan) indicating what he has gone to, and this is a necessary condition; so everyone who calls upon other than Allah has no proof for that. Rather, the proofs have demonstrated the falsehood of what he has gone to, yet he turns away from them out of injustice and obstinacy. Such a person will come before his Lord, and He will recompense him for his deeds, and he will attain nothing of success (falah), because he is a disbeliever. ﴿Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.﴾ Their disbelief prevented them from success.

{118} ﴿And say﴾: calling upon your Lord, sincere to Him in religion: ﴿My Lord, forgive﴾: us, so that You may save us from what is disliked, and have mercy upon us, so that through Your mercy You may bring us to every good. ﴿And You are the best of the merciful.﴾ Every merciful one shows mercy to the servant, but Allah is better for him than that, more merciful to His servant than a mother to her child, and more merciful to him than he is to himself.

The commentary on Surat al-Mu'minun is completed by His grace and bounty.
